one_line: Maratha architect-engineer of Raigad and the coastal-hill fort network in the Sahyadris.

appearance.age_look: Early 40s, lean but sturdy build, the wiry strength of a field engineer used to climbing forts and measuring rocky slopes.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones, medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache and short boxed beard; a faint old scar on the left eyebrow; default expression is calm, observant focus with a slight, knowing half-smile as if assessing terrain.
appearance.hair: Thick dark brown-black hair, tied back into a low knot at the nape beneath a deep saffron Maratha-style pagadi (turban) with a modest central fold and a narrow dark green cloth band wrapped once around the base, no ornament.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate mid-17th-century Maratha attire: a long, knee-length white cotton angarkha with overlapping front panels and subtle narrow grey stripes, tied at the right with fabric cords; beneath it, a light cream cotton kurta collar visible at the neck; deep indigo-blue churidar-style trousers gathered neatly at the ankles; a sturdy, slightly faded maroon cotton patka (waist sash) wrapped twice around his waist with the loose end tucked at the left hip; simple brown leather sandals suited to rocky fort steps; over one shoulder, a plain undyed cotton shawl (off-white, slightly textured) that engineers can use for shade or as a measuring rope; minimal jewellery—only a thin dark metal bangle on his right wrist and a small, unobtrusive black-thread armlet under the angarkha sleeve hinting at regional custom.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf measuring cord and survey kit: a cylindrical wooden case slung across his back by a dark leather strap, from which protrudes a rolled palm-leaf map; in his right hand he carries a straight wooden surveying staff marked with simple burnt-in measurement lines, while a short, sheathed straight tulwar with a plain iron hilt hangs from his left hip, more as a practical sidearm than a showpiece.

ref_desc: Hiroji Indulkar is a wiry early-40s Maratha engineer with an oval medium-brown face, trimmed moustache and beard, saffron pagadi, white striped angarkha over indigo churidar, maroon waist sash, off-white shawl, leather sandals, and a wooden surveying staff with palm-leaf map case plus plain sheathed tulwar.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Hiroji Indulkar, a dignified mid-17th-century Maratha fort engineer: in his early 40s, lean and wiry, medium-brown Deccan complexion, oval face, high cheekbones, straight nose, faint scar on the left eyebrow, neatly trimmed moustache and short boxed beard, default expression calm and assessing with a slight, knowing half-smile. His thick dark brown-black hair is tied in a low knot at the nape, covered by a deep saffron Maratha-style pagadi (turban) with a simple central fold and a narrow dark green band at the base. He wears a knee-length white cotton angarkha with subtle narrow grey stripes and overlapping front panels tied on the right, a cream kurta collar just visible at the neck, and deep indigo-blue churidar trousers gathered cleanly at the ankles. Around his waist is a sturdy maroon cotton patka (sash) wrapped twice, the loose end tucked at his left hip, with a short plain sheathed straight tulwar hanging slightly angled from a belt, clearly secondary to his tools. Over one shoulder lies an undyed off-white cotton shawl, slightly textured, draping modestly over his torso, and on his feet are simple brown leather sandals suitable for rocky hill-fort steps. His only visible jewellery is a thin dark metal bangle on his right wrist. His signature props are a straight wooden surveying staff with burnt-in measurement marks held in his right hand and a cylindrical wooden case slung across his back on a dark leather strap, the end of a rolled palm-leaf map protruding clearly. Use a restrained palette of white, indigo blue, maroon, saffron, and dark brown, and show him from multiple angles to emphasize the consistent turban shape, striped angarkha, indigo churidar, maroon sash, shawl, sandals, surveying staff, and map case with tulwar at his hip.
